From 2537089413514caaa9a5fdeeac3a34d45100f747 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Zilin Guan <zilin@seu.edu.cn>
Date: Mon, 26 Jan 2026 08:11:21 +0000
Subject: [PATCH] i3c: dw: Fix memory leak in dw_i3c_master_i2c_xfers()

The dw_i3c_master_i2c_xfers() function allocates memory for the xfer
structure using dw_i3c_master_alloc_xfer(). If pm_runtime_resume_and_get()
fails, the function returns without freeing the allocated xfer, resulting
in a memory leak.

Add a dw_i3c_master_free_xfer() call to the error path to ensure the
allocated memory is properly freed.

Compile tested only. Issue found using a prototype static analysis tool
and code review.

Fixes: 62fe9d06f570 ("i3c: dw: Add power management support")
Signed-off-by: Zilin Guan <zilin@seu.edu.cn>
Reviewed-by: Frank Li <Frank.Li@nxp.com>
Link: https://patch.msgid.link/20260126081121.644099-1-zilin@seu.edu.cn
Signed-off-by: Alexandre Belloni <alexandre.belloni@bootlin.com>

diff --git a/drivers/i3c/master/dw-i3c-master.c b/drivers/i3c/master/dw-i3c-master.c
index e9b2c23ed171..cfc15aaf8c7b 100644
--- a/drivers/i3c/master/dw-i3c-master.c
+++ b/drivers/i3c/master/dw-i3c-master.c
@@ -1106,6 +1106,7 @@ static int dw_i3c_master_i2c_xfers(struct i2c_dev_desc *dev,
 		dev_err(master->dev,
 			"<%s> cannot resume i3c bus master, err: %d\n",
 			__func__, ret);
+		dw_i3c_master_free_xfer(xfer);
 		return ret;
 	}
 
-- 
2.34.1

The patch fixes a memory leak in `dw_i3c_master_i2c_xfers()` within `drivers/i3c/master/dw-i3c-master.c`. Specifically, it adds a call to `dw_i3c_master_free_xfer(xfer)` in the error path after a failed `pm_runtime_resume_and_get()` call, ensuring that the previously allocated transfer structure is freed before returning.

**Modifications per file:**
- **drivers/i3c/master/dw-i3c-master.c**: Added one line (`dw_i3c_master_free_xfer(xfer);`) inside the error handling block for the failed `pm_runtime_resume_and_get()` call.

**Relationships:** The change is isolated to a single file and function. The error path is extended to release the `xfer` allocation, which had been overlooked, directly fixing the memory leak without affecting other code paths.
